Tessa / Silverpine —

Putting some initial technical guidance here so expectations are set before we run the jobs: 

- AWQ (6B)
  * Pros: usually the best size/throughput trade for CPU-constrained or small GPU footprints; AES-style per-channel scaling improves FP16-like fidelity at 4-bit, often with minimal perceptible QA regressions on factual tasks.
  * Cons: can require per-layer calibration and sometimes backfills larger residual errors on instruction-following edge cases.
  * Expected: ~2.5x throughput vs 13B GPTQ at comparable latency budget on a V100-class GPU in our test harness.

- GPTQ (13B)
  * Pros: retains more headroom for long-context coherence and fewer edge hallucinations in multi-turn tests; better for tasks needing broader knowledge.
  * Cons: higher memory and slower per-token throughput; quant artifacts can appear if calibration set isn't representative.
  * Expected: ~1x baseline throughput (relative) but quality headroom.

- FP8 (experimental)
  * Pros: great throughput and lower VRAM; promising for batch offline summarization workloads.
  * Cons: still early; expect more variance in QA accuracy unless we constrain sequence lengths and apply selective higher-precision layers.

Recommended evaluation matrix (what we'll run):
- Baselines: FP16 runs for Llama-2-13B-chat and Redwood-6B (unquantized).
- Quant runs: AWQ @ 4-bit on Redwood-6B; GPTQ @ 4-bit on Llama-2-13B; FP8 variant on Redwood-6B for offline batch jobs.
- Metrics: end-to-end latency (p95), tokens/sec, token-level accuracy on Silverpine QA set, and a small prompt-sensitivity regression test (n=200).
- Deliverables: CSV with per-model metrics + short recommendation (model, quant profile, expected $/1M tokens).

I'll seed the benchmarking pipeline Friday; Neha can help with the prompt-sensitivity sweep and automated comparisons.

Sergio

Adding the prompt-sensitivity specifics and a quick checklist for the PoC engineers: 

Prompt-sensitivity sweep plan:
- Use the 3 priority templates A/B/C. For each template, run the following perturbations: truncation (drop last 20% tokens), paraphrase (3 variants), prefix noise (insert 1 random sentence), and context-shift (swap user context).
- Track: exact-match, F1 on entities, and subjective factuality score (annotated by Silverpine sample of 100).

PoC run checklist for Redwood engineers:
- Ingest the 1k prompt slice and your full QA set (Silverpine) into a private test workspace.
- Run baselines (FP16) first; then run quant variants in parallel.
- Generate CSV: model, quant_profile, p50/p95 latency, tokens_sec, exact_match, f1, subjective_factuality, notes.

I'll own the prompt-sensitivity harness and the regression comparison scripts. Sergio, can you include a short note about calibration sample size we should use for GPTQ (recommendation: 2k tokens per layer sample or equivalent)?
